 JUDGMENT
The petitioner has filed this petition under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, claiming compensation of Rs.12,00,000/- for the injuries sustained by him in a road traffic accident.

The brief facts of the petitioner's case are as under:
2.

That on 18.8.2022 at about 2.30 p.m. the petitioner was proceeding in a motor cycle bearing registration No. KA-42-U-2994 along with pillion on the extreme left side of Lakshmipura-Uddandahalli main road, slowly and cautiously by observing all the traffic rules and regulations, when they reached opposite to Kitti Farm,
Uddandahalli, Tavarekere Hobli, Bengaluru City, suddenly, driver of the Borewell repairing Jeep bearing registration No.KA- 18-9425 drove the same with high speed in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the motor cycle.
Due to the said impact, petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries.

3. It is further stated that, immediately the petitioner was shifted to Supra Hospital, Bengalruru wherein he was treated as an inpatient and had spent Rs.2,00,000/- towards medicines, attendant charges, food and nourishment etc.

4. It is also stated in the petition that, prior to the accident the petitioner was hale and healthy, aged about 23 years, working as a driver and earning a sum of Rs.20,000/- per month and he used to spend the said amount for the maintenance of his family members.
After the accident, he could not do any work due to his severe injuries.
5. It is alleged in the petition that, the accident was occurred due to the rash and negligent act of the driver of the car bearing No.KA-18-9425.
In this regard, case was registered against the driver by the jurisdictional Tavarekere Police in Crime No.295/2022 under section 279 and 338 of IPC.

As such,
the respondent No.1 being the owner and the respondent No.2 being the insurance company of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
Hence, the petitioner has filed the instant petition seeking compensation.
6. In response to the notices, the respondents have appeared through their respective counsel and filed the written statements.

7. In the written statement of the respondent No.1 has contended that the accident occurred due to the negligence of the petitioner as the petitioner drink and drive the vehicle and himself hit the front of the right side stopped Bore well Jeep, the petitioner uncontrolled the bike and fell down.

Further Parashuram vs Gangarevaiah on 12 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/83381240/
2 contended that the petitioner not intimated in time and tried to hide the drunken facts and reported lately after more than 24 hours and created all fabricated document.

With all these main grounds, prayed to dismiss the petition with cost.
8.
In the written statement, the respondent No.2 has not seriously disputed the accident and the injuries sustained by the petitioner.

It is the contention of the respondent that, petition is bad for non-joinder of necessary parties and the rider of the motor cycle bearing No.KA-42-U-2994 has rode the vehicle, without wearing helmet and without driving licence.
Further contended that the driver Gangararevaiah was driving the Jeep bearing No.KA- 18-9425 who did not had valid and effective driving licence to drive the same.

It is also contention of the respondent No.2 that police instead of filing charge sheet against Gangarevaiah falsely implicated his son Madhu P.G. that on the date of accident Madhu was driver of the Jeep bearing No.KA-18-9425.
Since the Gangarevaiah did not had valid and effective driving licence.
Respondent No.2 admitted about the issuance of policy in respect of Jeep bearing No.KA-18-9425 and the liability of this respondent is subject to terms and conditions of the policy.
It is also contention of the respondent that, the accident occurred due to the negligence of the rider of the motor cycle bearing No.KA-42-U-2994 and not on the part of the driver of the car.
Ultimately stated that, the compensation claimed by the petitioner is highly excessive, exorbitant and without any basis.
With all these main grounds, prayed to dismiss the petition with cost.

9. On the basis of rival pleadings of both the parties, this court has framed the following issues;
ISSUES 1) Whether the petitioner proves that, he had sustained grievous injuries in a motor vehicle accident,
that was taken place on 18.8.2022 at about 2.30 p.m. on Lakshmipura-Uddandahalli main road,
near Kitti farm, Uddandahalli, Tavarekere Hobli, Bengaluru, due to the rash and negligent driver of Bore well repairing Jeep of the rider of the motor cycle bearing registration No.KA-18-9425, in an actionable negligence?
2) Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation as prayed for?

If so, at what rate? from whom?
3) What order or award?
10.
In order to substantiate the case of the petitioner, he himself examined as PW1 and got marked as Ex.P1 to Ex.P11.
In addition this, placed the evidence of Dr.Nagaraj B.N. as PW2 and got marked the documents at Ex.P12 & Ex.P13.

Apart from his evidence, placed the evidence of Medical Record Technician as PW3 and got marked at Ex.P14 to Ex.P18.
11.
On the other hand, the respondent No.1 has examined as RW1 and got marked the documents at Ex.R1 to Ex.R8.

13. My answer to the aforesaid issues are as follows:
 Issue No.1: In the Affirmative.

Issue No.2: Partly in the Affirmative.
 Issue No.3:

As per final order,

 R E A S O N S ISSUE NO.1:-
14.

It is the specific case of the petitioner that, due to the actionable negligence on the part of the driver of the Borewell Jeep bearing registration No.KA-18-9425, the alleged accident had taken place, consequently he had sustained grievous injuries.

15. On the other hand, the respondents being the owner and the insurance company, though not disputed the accident and the injuries sustained by the petitioner, seriously disputed the manner of accident.
In the light of the rival contentions of both the parties, on going through the above issue burden is on the petitioner to prove the above issue on the touch stone of preponderance of probabilities.
16. The petitioner in order to prove his case, examined himself as PW1.
In his examination-in- chief by way of affidavit has reiterated the averments made in the petition.
The petitioner in support of his oral evidence has relied upon Ex.
P1 to P6
. Ex.P1- true copy of the F.I.R. in Crime No.295/2022 of Tavarekere Police Station.
Ex.P2-true copy of the first information statement given by the petitioner.
Ex.P3-true copy of the mahazar.
Ex.P4-true copy of the IMV report, Ex.P5-wound certificate of the petitioner.
Ex . P6
-true copy of the charge sheet in Crime No.295/2022 of Tavarekere Police.

17. On perusal of the police documents, it could be seen that, based upon the first information statement given by the petitioner, the S.H.O. of Tavarekere Police has registered the case against the driver of the offending vehicle for the offences punishable under Sections 279 and 337 of I.P.C.

Upon investigation, the I.O. has filed charge sheet against the driver of the offending vehicle alleging that he has committed the offences punishable under section 279, 337 and 338 of IPC & Section 187 of IMV Act.
18.
The respondent No.2 has contended that as on the date of the accident respondent No.1 Gangarevaiah was driving the vehicle as he had no valid driving licence.

Hence, police have implicated his son Madhu, who being the driver of the Borewell Jeep bearing No.KA-18-9425.
19.
In answer to the contention of the respondent No.2, the respondent No.1 has examined as RW1.
He has stated in his evidence that he being the owner of the offending vehicle and the policy was valid as on the date of the accident.
Madhu P.G. was working under hima s a driver.
At the time of accident he was driving the vehicle and he had valid and effective driving licence.

20. RW1 has been cross
- examined by respondent No.2, but nothing has been elciited from his mouth to prove that as on the date of accident RW1 was the driver and he has implicated his son Madhu P.G. as a driver.
21. Further, to prove the defense of the rash and negligenct act of the petitioner with drunk and drive, no convincing documents placed on record for consideration.

Either to examine the driver of the offending vehicle or any of the independent witnesses who witnessed the alleged accident to prove that due to the actionable negligence on the part of the petitioner, the accident was occurred.

22. Though the PW1 was subjected to cross- examination at length, nothing has been elicited from the mouth of the PW1 that this accident is not due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending vehicle.

From the oral evidence of the PW1 coupled with the police documents at Ex.P1 to Ex.P6, it is no doubt that the petitioner has sustained injuries in the accident which is result of rash and negligent driving of the driver of the Bore well Jeep bearing registration No.KA-18-9425.

Hence,
issue No.1 is answered in the Affirmative.

ISSUE NO.2 :
23.
This issue is with respect to the entitlement of reliefs claimed by the petitioner.
The petitioner through this petition, claiming compensation of Rs.12,00,000/- on account of the injuries sustained by him in the accident under different heads.

24. Before appreciation of the evidence placed by the petitioner about the injuries sustained by him,
in the accident and its consequences, it is apt to note herein, the preposition laid down in the following land mark judgment, while appreciating the injury cases in Motor Vehicle Act.
Civil Appeal No.8981/2010 D.D. 18.10.2010 Rajkumar V/s Ajay Kumar & Another of the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India.
"In the aforesaid case, it was held that, the court has to make judicious attempt to award compensation to the loss suffered by the claimant.
The compensation should not be assessed conservatively.
On the other hand, compensation should also not be endeavouring to secure some uniformity and consistency.
The object of awarding compensation is to make good the loss suffered as a result of wrong done, as far as money can do so, in a fair reasonable and equitable manner."

"while determining quantum of compensation, in such cases, the court has to strike a balance between the inflated and unreasonable demands of a victim and the equally untenable claim of the opposite party saying that nothing is payable.
That sympathy for the victim does not, and should not, comes in the way of making a correct assessment.
But if a case is made out, and the court must not be chary of awarding adequate compensation. "

sentences.text: PW1 has stated in his evidence that, he has sustained the injuries in a road traffic accident.
In connection with the injuries he has produced wound certificate marked as Ex.P5.

The said document discloses that, he had sustained the following injuries:-
1) Abrasion lower and upper extrative 2) Fracture of left leg tibia and fibula 3) Fracture of left foot calcaneus 26.
In connection with the above said injuries, the doctor is of the opinion that the injury No.2 & 3 are grievous in nature and the injury No.1 is simple in nature.
Further, the petitioner has produced discharge summary as per Ex.P9.
On going through the discharge summary issued by Supra Hopital, Bengaluru reveals that, the petitioner was admitted from 18.8.2022 to 22.8.2022.
In addition to his evidence, placed the evidence of Dr.Nagaraj B.N. as PW2.

PW2 has stated in his evidence that the petitioner has sustained comminuted fracture of left leg both bones with fracture of the left calcaneus and placed clinical note & x-ray as per Ex.P12 & Ex.P13.
Apart from his evidence placed the evidence of medical record technician of Supra Hospital as PW3.

He has placed MLC,
case sheet, x-rays, police intimation and authorisation letteras per Ex.P14 to Ex.P18.

By taking into consideration of the nature of the injuries and the treatment taken by the petitioner, he could have undergone pain and sufferings while taking treatment, as an in patient as well as an outpatient.
Hence, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.50,000/- under the head of Pain and Sufferings.

Loss of income during treatment period:
27.
PW1 has stated that, he was working as a driver and was earning a sum of Rs.20,000/- per month.
There is no iota of documents to prove that he was earning Rs.20,000/- per month.
In such a situation, as per law, notional income has to be taken.
On going through the discharge summary of Supra Hopital, Bengaluru marked at Ex.P9 reveals that, the petitioner was admitted from 18.8.2022 to 22.8.2022.

During the period of treatment, definitely, there was some difficulty to him to do daily routine work and to do his work for livelihood at least for a period of two months by looking in to the nature of the injuries sustained by him.
Hence, I am of the view that, it is just and proper to award compensation of Rs.31,000/- towards loss of income during the laid up period and rest period.

Medical Expeneses;
28.
The petitioner in connection with his treatment expenses, at the time of his evidence, placed medical bills of Rs.1,22,479/- as per Ex.P11 along with prescriptions as per Ex.P11.
At the time of cross-examination except the suggestion that the medical bills are created, nothing has been placed on record to prove that the medical bills are created for the purpose of this case.

Hence, the Parashuram vs Gangarevaiah on 12 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/83381240/
6 petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.1,22,479/- towards medical expenses.

sentences.text:
Attendant charges, food and nourishment and conveyance charges;
29.

The petitioner herein, as per the medical records and also on going through the discharge summary the petitioner has taken treatment as an inpatient and as an outpatient, definitely the petitioner could have spent some amount towards, food, nourishment, conveyance, as well as towards attendant charges.

Hence, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.10,000/-
towards attendant charges, food, nourishment and conveyance charges.

Loss of future income;
30.
The petitioner herein, asserting that, he had sustained permanent disability, consequent upon the injuries sustained by him.
In order to prove the same, the petitioner has relied on his evidence along with the wound certificate and other medical documents.

In the evidence of the PW1,
reiterated the same thing forthcoming in the main petition.
As already discussed above, wound certificate placed by him as per Ex.P5 goes to show that, he had sustained grievous injuries.
To substantiate this, the petitioner had placed discharge summary for consideration.

Apart from this,
another material witness by name Dr.Nagaraj B.N. examined as PW2.
PW2 has stated in his evidence that the petitioner has sustained comminuted fracture of left leg both bones with fracture of the left calcaneus.
For which the petitioner was treated with ORIF with IMIL nailing of the tibia and K wire for the calcaneus on 19.8.2022 and later he was discharged with regular follow-up treatment.
31. PW2 has stated that, at the time of his examination the petitioner has swollen left heel, restricted left ankle and knee movements.
X-ray shows united fracture with implant in situ.
The petitioner has placed clinical note and x-ray as per Ex.P12 & Ex.P13.

On the basis of entire evaluation of the disability of the petitioner, PW2 had opined that, total physical disability of left lower limb is 42%
and that of his whole body at 14%.

In support of his evidence produced clinical note and x-ray as per Ex.P12 & Ex.P13.
32.
At the time of cross-examination of PW2, admitted that he is not treated doctor.
Fracture is united.
Based on the documents he has assessed the physical disability.
This witness also denied the suggestion that, he assessed the disability of the petitioner on higher side.
33. Over all appreciation of evidence of PW2 along with the entire medical documents the whole body disability expressed by PW2 seems to be right.
Hence, by taking into consideration of point of disability expressed by PW2, it is apt to take whole body disability as 14%.
The same will meets the ends of justice.
34. In connection with the age of the petitioner is concerned, on going through the cause title of the petition reveals that, as on the date of the petition, his age was 23 years.

In support of the age proof,
he has placed driving licence and Aadhar card marked at Ex.P7 & Ex.P8 for consideration.
On going through the said documents, the date of birth of the petitioner has been mentioned as 7.6.2000.

The Parashuram vs Gangarevaiah on 12 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/83381240/
7 accident occurred on 18.8.2022.

sentences.text: Therefore, as on the date of accident, the age of the petitioner is considered as 22 years.

To the said age as per Sarla Verma case, multiplier '18' is to be taken into consideration.
35.

Next factual aspect of the income of the petitioner is concerned, in his evidence the petitioner has stated that, prior to the accident, he was working as a driver and getting an income of Rs.20,000/- per month.
There is no iota of documents to prove his income.
In such a situation, as per law notional income has to be taken into consideration.
But the said notional income is to be taken judiciously, by taking into consideration of the year of the accident.

It is pertinent to note that,
in the case on hand, the alleged accident had taken place in the year 2022.
As per the notional income chart, I am of the view that, it is apt to take the notional income of the petitioner as Rs.15,500/- for the year 2022.

36. In the light of my detailed discussions held above, no doubt injuries sustained by the petitioner,
definitely come in the way of his future, in a slight manner, to do his daily routine work, as well as to do his work for livelihood on going through his age criteria.

Hence, the petitioner herein, is entitled for compensation under loss of future income as follows:
Rs.15,500 X 12 X 18 X14/100= Rs.4,68,720/-.
Loss of amenities;
37.

PW1 has stated in his evidence that due to the accidental injuries he cannot walk for long distance, he cannot sit, squat, cannot use Indian toilet and undergoing deep mental shock, since the injuries caused are permanent in nature.

On perusal of evidence of PW2 and also medical documents, I am of the view that, the petitioner will suffer a slight problem in future also, to do his normal work, as well as his work for livelihood as a mason.
Hence, it is just and proper to award compensation of Rs.20,000/- towards loss of amenities.
38. In connection with the future medication, PW2 has stated that petitioner needs another surgery for removal of implant, the estimate of this surgery is Rs.60,000/-.
Relying on the opinion of the doctor it is just and proper to award compensation of Rs.20,000/- under the head of future medical expenses.

39. In view of my discussions held above, on various aspects the petitioner is entitled for compensation in to to, under the following heads:
Compensation heads Compensation amount 1.Pain and Suffering Rs. 50,000-00 2.Loss of income during Rs. 31,000-00 laid-up period and rest period 3.

Medical expenses Rs.1,22,479-00 Parashuram vs Gangarevaiah on 12 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/83381240/
8 4. Attendant, Nourishment Rs. 10,000-00 and Conveyance Charges 5. Loss of future income Rs.4,68,720-00 due to disability 6. Loss of Amenities Rs. 20,000-00 7.
Future medication Rs. 20,000-00 Total Rs.7,22,199-00 40.

Accordingly, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.7,22,199/- (Rupees seven lakh twenty two thousand one hundred and ninety nine only), along with interest @ 6% per annum, as per the proposition laid down by the Honourable High court of Karnataka in, MFA No.103557/2016,
between Sri Ram General Insurance Company Limited V/S. Lakshmi And Others dated. 20.03.2018.
And MFA No.30131/2019 dated.12.5.2020, from the date of the petition, till the realization of the award amount.

LIABILITY:
41.

As regards the liability is concerned, it is the assertion of the petitioner that, due to the actionable negligence on the part of the driver of the Borewell repairing Jeep bearing registration No.KA- 18-9425, alleged accident had taken place.
The evidence given by the petitioner in connection with the issue No.1, remained unshaken.

As such, it is the strong assertion of the petitioner that, the respondent No.1 being the owner and the respondent No.2 being the insurance company of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.
42. As per the records insurance policy was valid from 9.4.2022 to 8.4.2023.
The alleged accident had taken place on 18.8.2022.
Ex.R3- policy copy also reveals the same.

As such, I am of the view that, the respondent No.1 being the owner and the respondent No.2 being the insurance company of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.

In view of the valid insurance policy, the respondent No.2 is liable to pay the compensation with interest at 6%
p.a. from the date of petition, till its realization.
Accordingly, I am answering the issue No.2 partly in the Affirmative.

ISSUE NO.3:
43.

In view of above discussions on issue Nos.1 & 2, I proceed to pass the following;
O R D E R
The claim petition filed by the petitioner U/s 166 of M.V. Act is partly allowed with cost.

The petitioner is entitled for  compensation of Rs.7,22,199/- (Rupees  seven lakh twenty two thousand one hundred and ninety nine only), along with interest @ 6% per annum, from the date of the petition till the realization of the award amount.

9
The respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation.

In view of the valid insurance policy, the respondent No.2 is liable to pay the compensation with interest at 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization within two months from the date of this order.
The expenses to be incurred for future medication shall not carry any interest.
After deposit of the compensation amount with interest, 40% is directed to be deposited in any Nationalized/Scheduled bank in F.D for a period of 3 years.
And remaining 60% shall be released to the petitioner through due process of law.
Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1000/-.
Draw award accordingly.
